sources.title: Lénaïc Chizat and Francis Bach, On the Global Convergence of Gradient Descent for Over-parameterized Models using Optimal Transport
sources.locator: Assumptions 2.1 and Definitions 2.2/2.4, printed pp. 3–5; Propositions 2.3/2.5 and Theorems 2.6/3.3/3.5, printed pp. 4–8; Appendix A and B.2.1–B.3, PDF pp. 12–22, and Appendix C.1–C.4, PDF pp. 23–26.

contents.name: Assumptions 2.1 and Definitions 2.2/2.4
contents.support: The carrier restates the complete regularity, cutoff, measure-energy and continuity-equation conventions. The velocity is corrected to the constrained negative minimum-norm subgradient on general convex Ω.

contents.name: Proposition 2.3 and Proposition 2.5
contents.support: The local Hilbert-lift proof is authored here; the source proposition is context only and is not used as a logical supplier.

contents.name: Theorem 2.6 and Appendix B.3 particle limit
contents.support: The present proof route uses a common-label coupling and localized W2 stability; it does not use the source’s compactness passage for velocity fields.

contents.name: Appendix B.2.1, Lemmas B.2–B.4
contents.support: The generalized-geodesic Taylor inequality is reproved locally from the lifted gradient bound; no external theorem is imported.

contents.name: Theorems 3.3/3.5 separation discussion
contents.support: Only the topological separation condition is illustrated; no global-optimality conclusion or unsupported activation example is asserted.

contents.name: Mixture versus displacement convexity
contents.support: The explicit sine-feature energy gives a direct counterexample to inferring displacement convexity from mixture convexity.

read_evidence.inspection: Full paper text fetched and inspected; the complete arguments at the listed sections were read. This records the relevant paper sections, not a claim that every page was studied in equal detail.

sources.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures
sources.locator: Chapter 4, Theorem 4.0.4 and §§4.1–4.3, printed pp. 77–98; Chapter 10, Definitions 10.3.1/10.3.2 and Proposition 10.4.2, printed pp. 275–287; Chapter 11, Theorem 11.2.1 and proof, printed pp. 299–305; Chapter 8, §§8.2–8.4, printed pp. 179–194.

contents.name: Chapter 4, Theorem 4.0.4 and §§4.1–4.3
contents.support: The resolvent, action estimates, limit inclusion, energy identity, minimum-norm selection and contraction are authored locally; the AGS theorem is not a premise.

contents.name: Chapter 10, Definitions 10.3.1/10.3.2 and Proposition 10.4.2
contents.support: The exact strong-subgradient and potential-subdifferential interfaces were read; the model-specific pointwise identity is reproved locally.

contents.name: Chapter 11, Theorem 11.2.1 and proof
contents.support: The full theorem proof and hypotheses were inspected as context. The AGS theorem is not a logical premise; the local G1 chain-rule proof remains escalated at Step 4.1.

contents.name: Chapter 8, Theorem 8.2.1 and Theorem 8.3.1
contents.support: The batch 50 superposition and continuity-equation interfaces are consumed after their actual draft bodies were inspected; they are not treated as independently accepted.

read_evidence.inspection: Full-text PDF fetched and inspected; the complete arguments at the listed theorems and sections were read. This records those relevant portions, not a claim to have read all 342 pages in full.
